clues: This town sits in the far east of Brazil. Its shores meet the Atlantic Ocean.
No town in Brazil gets more rain in a year. Its yearly rain is the highest in the whole country.
Early in the 1900s, Brazil carved this mining coast into four zones. That old mining plan still sets this town apart.
An old stone observatory stands here. Its builders raised huge stones to watch the sky.
One bold nickname sums up its most famous sight. People call that sight the Amazon Stonehenge.
